origin.description: Lorenz curve of the lognormal distribution, with one scale parameter.

arguments.name: p
arguments.text: Population shares in the unit interval.

arguments.name: parameter
arguments.text: Log-standard-deviation. The default is 1, and only the first element is used.

origin.details: Shares of 0 and 1 stay at 0 and 1. Every other share is passed through the standard normal quantile, shifted by the parameter, and mapped back with the standard normal distribution function. A non-positive parameter warns and is replaced by 1. The function has class theorLc.

translation.description: Lorenz curve of the lognormal distribution, with one scale parameter.

arguments.name: p
arguments.text: Population shares in the unit interval, as a scalar or an array.

arguments.name: parameter
arguments.text: Log-standard-deviation. The default is 1. A sequence contributes its first element.

translation.details: Endpoints stay fixed. Interior shares use the standard normal quantile and distribution function, with the normal probability taken from the error function. A parameter that is not strictly positive warns and is replaced by 1. The result keeps the shape of p.
translation.value: Lorenz ordinates at p, as a NumPy array of the same shape.
translation.example:
import numpy as np
from ineq.theor import lc_lognorm

p = np.arange(1, 11) / 10
print(lc_lognorm(p, parameter=0.78))
